A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmarks, Text-Attr, and Taxon-SSL. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched despite extensive restructuring.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments, label-sparsity studies, ablations, representation analyses, and consistency-based inference results in Section 5 and Appendices C–E.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds irregular-hierarchy experiments, text-encoder and caption comparisons, and a stopping-rule comparison.

M1.justification: Equation 4 removes v1's outer sum over hierarchy levels from the taxonomy-aligned contrastive loss, changing its written scaling. The core architectures, caption supervision, pseudo-label affinity construction, and consistency-based stopping remain. The PDFs do not establish whether this formula revision changed the implementation; the expanded SSL description mainly documents the existing method.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix C adds evaluation on an ImageNet mammal subtree with irregular five-to-ten-level WordNet paths, extending coverage to structurally irregular prediction targets. The five existing free-grain benchmarks and their curated taxonomies remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds confidence-based stopping as a comparator to consistency-based inference and a simple class-label text baseline against image-specific captions. HRN, H-CAST, and the existing method combinations remain in their corresponding benchmark comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include anchoring irregular-hierarchy leaves at Level 10, excluding trivial single-class levels from reporting, and comparing stopping rules using confidence threshold 0.9 selected from [0.85, 0.99]. Encoder and caption substitutions introduce additional experimental controls. Existing benchmark metrics, sparsity ratios, and 100/200-epoch budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands the questions tested: Appendix C examines robustness to irregular taxonomy structure; Appendix F.3 tests dependence on CLIP versus SigLIP and E5; Appendix F.5 tests instance-specific captions against class prompts; and Section 5.4 compares stopping strategies. Earlier sparsity, saliency, t-SNE, loss-weight, scheduling, and layer-placement analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds, average performance, and the same stated variance range of 0.1–1.8 for randomized sparsity experiments. V2 adds no new repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. V2 reports irregular-hierarchy Level-10 accuracy of 63.5% for H-CAST versus 67.7% for Text-Attr; encoder FPAs of 63.2/62.9/61.8 for CLIP/SigLIP/E5; and caption FPAs of 62.0 versus 63.2 for simple versus image-specific text. Figure 8 adds 48% versus 63% reaching the fine level correctly under confidence versus consistency stopping. These are newly reported comparisons, not performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Equation 4 removes a hierarchy-level sum whose summand did not depend on that level. Appendix H also explicitly defines the confidence-gated pseudo-label loss and combined training objective. The underlying label-availability assumptions remain, and neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V1 already explores consistency-based inference, but v2 incorporates adaptive prediction depth into the stated task and contribution list. It adds the core comparative claim that consistency-based stopping yields deeper correct predictions than confidence-based stopping. The benchmark and two training-method contributions remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations involving sibling-class probability splitting, semantic misalignment and sparse supervision in irregular hierarchies, and the benefits of instance-specific text across encoders. It also treats Rosch's categories as guidance rather than strict definitions and explicitly discusses improving CLIP-based pruning. Earlier interpretations of dataset-dependent method strengths remain.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information through Appendix H's full SSL objective, weak/strong augmentation procedure, percentile-based confidence schedule, and loss weights. It adds detailed taxonomy-construction guidance, alternative encoder configurations, and caption-generation cost of approximately 2.1 seconds per image on an A40. Code and data change from promised availability to stated availability; existing main training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references concerning hierarchical failures of vision-language models, annotation constraints, and the newly tested text encoders. It expands distinctions from FineR and CHMatch while removing some earlier cognitive-taxonomy and benchmark citations. The central positioning relative to hierarchical, weakly supervised, and long-tailed recognition remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around training and inference. Methods and experiments gain reorganized subsections, related work moves to the final appendix, and dataset construction and complete SSL losses receive dedicated appendices. The title adds 'Visual.' These changes substantially revise the narrative beyond accommodating new experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two, with a new introductory task schematic and extensive figure rearrangement. V1's main results table becomes part of v2 Figure 5, and the class-index accuracy plot becomes a scatter plot. Hierarchy illustrations are merged or relocated, and new stopping, robustness, encoder, and caption displays are added.

improvement.justification: The new hierarchy, encoder, and caption controls strengthen support for the existing methods, while fuller SSL documentation and caption-cost reporting improve reproducibility and practical assessment. The gains are bounded: principal benchmark results remain unchanged, the new stopping comparison covers ImageNet-F, and the loss-scaling revision is not linked to a documented implementation change. Overall, v2 provides better validation and transparency.
